newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China diesel prices steady, worries over imports.
newsitem.headline: China diesel prices steady, worries over imports.

text.p: Delivered prices of gas oil and fuel oil to south China hovered around previous week's quotes with bids/offers far apart amid weak demand, industry sources said on Friday.
They said oil trade between Hong Kong and China had slowed sharply, with traders forecasting a slump in imports.
"Diesel imports have reached a near halt since last week, it is as if there is a temporary ban on imports," said an oil trader in Hong Kong.
"We are not offering any cargoes as they are no demand at all," another trader, with a major oil firm in Hong Kong, said.
Earlier this month, Beijing placed restrictions on diesel imports by not issuing fresh import licences for the third quarter.
The curb was prompted by rising stocks in northern provinces and poor demand in the high energy consuming centres in the south.
The high stock levels were further exacerbated by cheaper smuggled imports, which were competing against oil sales from domestic refineries.
"I expect imports in August to tumble. Already in July Chinese buyers have retreated from the spot market," a local trader in Singapore said.
In June, China imported 875,461 tonnes of diesel, customs figures showed. In July imports is expected to be less, possibly below 600,000 tonnes and August would be even lower, said one trader.
"I do not expect diesel imports to pick up until the second half of August," the trader in Hong Kong said.
"Sellers can place any offers they want under the current market sentiment, as there are no buyers at all," the major oil trader in Hong Kong, said.
"A few July cargoes are being delivered currently but talk of August supplies were almost non-existant," he said.
Most traders in Hong Kong and China said oil imports would only pick up when state refiner, Sinopec, was happy with stock levels.
The 170,000 barrels-per-day Maoming refinery reduced runs by around 10-15 percent in mid July.
Export sales from South Korea to China were also slow, Korean refiners told Reuters.
South Korea supplies for August loading were offfered at a discount of 30 cents to Singapore spot quotes.
Fuel oil imports into South China were slow but steady, traders said.
"China is still taking in fuel oil but imports were slow," said a Japanese trader in Singapore.
A Japanese trader was heard to have sold a fuel oil cargo at $8 per tonne premium over Singapore spot quotes, c-and f South China last week for August delivery.
